title: Rational Inequalities
standard_text: P.5K solve rational inequalities with real coefficients by applying a variety of techniques and write the solution set of the rational inequality in interval notation in mathematical and real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Precalculus rational inequality worksheets for Texas TEKS P.5K: critical numbers, sign charts, solving in interval notation and real-world rational inequalities. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Critical numbers come from the top and the bottom.
key_sub: A zero of the denominator is never included.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Get 0 on one side and write one fraction. Do not multiply both sides by an expression with x: its sign can change.
  • Critical numbers are the zeros of the numerator and of the denominator.
  • Test one value in each interval to find the sign of the fraction.
  • Zeros of the numerator are included for ≤ and ≥; zeros of the denominator are never included.

Examples

Example

x − 3x + 1 ≤ 0

Critical numbers −1 and 3

Negative between them

Answer: (−1, 3]

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Including a zero of the denominatorIt makes the fraction undefined.
Multiplying by the denominatorSubtract and combine instead.
Forgetting the top's zerosBoth top and bottom give critical numbers.

faq.q: Why is the denominator's zero always open?
faq.a: The expression is not defined there.
Yes: look where the graph is above or below the x-axis.

faq.q: When can I multiply by the denominator?
faq.a: Only when you know it is positive, such as a number of items.

items.q: Is (x + 4)(x + 1) positive or negative when x = 8?
